title: Language-tag filter still fails open for alias tags (ts/py/cpp/golang)
description:
Review finding on sutra/280 (medium). The fix correctly derives LANGUAGE_CATEGORIES from default_registry().language_ids() = {rust, dart, c, python, javascript, typescript} and closes the case-asymmetry bug. But the fail-open default is unchanged.

`is_language_category` matches only exact adapter language_ids. A lesson tagged `ts`, `js`, `py`, `golang`, `cpp`, or any language sutra has no adapter for still yields `lang_tags.is_empty() == true` and passes unconditionally into every workspace — the exact mechanism sutra/280 was filed to kill, just narrower. `remember::enrich` seeds from `file.language` so sutra's own writes align, but caller-supplied tags do not have to.

Needs a design call before implementation, hence HITL. Two options:
(a) Alias table mapping common shorthands to adapter ids. Cheap, but an open-ended list that will keep missing entries — the same failure mode one level up.
(b) Flip the default: treat a tag that looks like a language claim but is unrecognized as a language claim (fail closed) rather than as language-neutral. Structurally correct, but needs a way to distinguish "language tag" from "any other category tag" without a recognition set — which is the hard part.

Recommend (b) with an explicit tag namespace (e.g. `lang:python`) so recognition is syntactic rather than dictionary-based, but that is a lessons schema/vocabulary change worth Josh's call.

acceptance_criteria.text: Design decision recorded on which strategy is taken and why
A lesson tagged with an unrecognized language shorthand does not leak into unrelated workspaces

decisions.decision: Move language claims into an explicit `lang:` tag namespace, applied by normalize_category() at write time, rather than extending the read-time recognition dictionary.
decisions.rationale: Makes the filter's question syntactic ('does the tag carry the prefix') instead of dictionary-based, so a language sutra has no adapter for still fails closed — it matches no workspace and stays out of all of them. The recognition dictionary survives only as a write-time convenience, where a miss mislabels one tag instead of leaking silently into every workspace. Also fixes the write/read asymmetry: recognition now happens once, at the point where the data is created.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: (a) An alias table mapping shorthands to adapter ids — cheaper and no migration, but it is the same open-ended dictionary one level up: the first unlisted language leaks exactly as before. (b) Naive fail-closed (treat any unrecognised tag as a language claim) — unworkable, because `categories` also carries topic tags seeded by remember::enrich (sqlite, grpc, observability), which would then be excluded from every workspace.

execution_record:
Landed as 2b04706. Blast radius was wider than the task described: two other readers of the categories table needed prefix-awareness — `sutra_lessons(category=...)`, which does an exact `c.tag = ?` (now normalises its argument through the same function as the writer, so `category="py"` finds `lang:python`), and sutra/279's search category tier, whose `tags_matching_query` splits on `-_.` and would no longer have matched a query for "rust" against `lang:rust` (now strips the prefix before token matching). Both were done in the same commit as the migration, since a partial rollout would have left the tier silently broken.

Migration 0007 uses UPDATE OR REPLACE rather than OR IGNORE: a lesson carrying both "Rust" and "rust" collides on UNIQUE(lesson_id, tag), and OR IGNORE would have left the loser behind unprefixed — precisely the row the migration exists to remove. The name list is frozen at the adapter set as of the migration on purpose; later adapters are handled on write.

Surprise during verification: a first pass over a `cp` of the live ~/.sutra/lessons.db reported 255 -> 239 rows, which looked like the migration deleting data. It was not — `cp` on a WAL-mode sqlite db drops whatever is still in the -wal file, and the 16 "lost" rows were the four newest lessons. Re-run via `sqlite3 ".backup"`: 255 -> 255, all 68 language rows rewritten, lossless. Stored as a lesson (019f8b15).

Verified: cargo test 1466 passed / 0 failed, clippy clean on --all-targets. Four enrichment-test assertions updated to the `lang:` form. Three new tests cover the alias case (`py` does not leak into rust), the unsupported-language case (`golang` and `lang:nim` leak nowhere), and prefix-transparency for both `category=` and the search tier.

Note for deployment: the migration applies when a binary built from this commit opens the db. The running MCP server is on the old binary and needs a reinstall/restart before the live lessons.db is rewritten.
root_cause: The Phase 3 workspace filter was subtractive and dictionary-driven: it excluded a lesson only when it recognised one of its category tags as a language name. Recognition and non-recognition therefore had opposite failure directions — an unrecognised tag (`py`, `golang`, any language without an adapter) produced an empty `lang_tags`, which the filter read as "this lesson makes no language claim" and passed into every workspace. Because `categories` is a single free-form bag carrying both language claims and topic tags (`sqlite`, `concurrency`), the filter had no way to tell "unrecognised language" from "topic tag", so no dictionary could ever make it fail closed.

messages.author: agent
messages.text:
Review (vidhi-review, reviewer=codex): request changes -> fixed in e96db99.

Codex verdict "needs-attention" on 2b04706, two findings, both real:

[high] Migration version-skew. 0007's rewrite list is frozen at the names known when it shipped and its content hash makes it unamendable, but normalize_category's dictionary is larger and will grow. A pre-existing bare `java`/`kotlin` row would stay unprefixed forever -- wrong in both directions at once: invisible to the Phase 3 filter (leaks into every workspace) and unreachable through `category=java`, which normalises its argument to `lang:java`. Fixed structurally rather than with another frozen list: `LessonsDb::normalize_stored_categories` runs the live normaliser over the categories table on open, so stored tags track the dictionary as it is rather than as it was at migration time. Idempotent -- topic tags normalise to themselves.

[medium] Bare `sql` converted from topic to unsupported-language claim. Found independently during the same pass, and worse than codex's version: this is not only a user typing "sql". `remember::enrich` emits `sql` as a technology tag from the `sqlx` import (IMPORT_TECH_MAP), so sutra's own auto-enrichment would have written `lang:sql` on every lesson anchored to sqlx-importing code, burying it in zero workspaces. sql/html/css/shell dropped from KNOWN_LANGUAGES; the rule is now "could a workspace *be* this language", with `lang:sql` still available for anyone who means the language. A unit test asserts no IMPORT_TECH_MAP value normalises to a language claim, so the two tables cannot collide again.

Also dropped the `node`->javascript alias (node is a runtime; mapping it to javascript would wrongly exclude node lessons from typescript workspaces) and `cs`->c# (ambiguous).

Verified: cargo test 1469 passed / 0 failed, clippy clean. Live db checked -- the one bare `sql` row is correctly left as a topic tag, and no rows exist in the un-migrated language set.

Codex did not flag: round-tripping/idempotency of normalize_category, the workspace-side canonicalisation path, Phase 3/Phase 4 ordering, the category-tier IN-clause binding, or test honesty. Those were in the focus text and came back clean.
